title: Production ML Decision Service
summary: A classical ML service that ties model quality to review capacity and financial cost: leakage checks, calibrated probabilities, cost-based thresholds, SHAP explanations, a model registry, and champion/challenger deployment.
primaryMessage: I connect classical machine-learning performance to operational capacity and financial consequences.

executive.problem: A team can review only so many flagged cases per day, and each missed case or needless review has a cost. A model tuned for accuracy alone ignores both.
executive.approach: Train a baseline and a candidate model on versioned data, calibrate their scores, pick the decision threshold from review capacity and cost, explain each decision, and deploy the challenger beside the champion before promotion.
executive.impact: The operating point is chosen in business terms, every prediction can be explained, and a model change is promoted only on evidence.
executive.whyItMatters: Shows mature classical ML: not only a good AUC, but the calibration, thresholds, monitoring, and deployment practice that make a model safe to depend on.

problem: Decision models such as risk or eligibility screening fail in production for reasons that offline accuracy hides: leakage inflates validation scores, class imbalance distorts thresholds, uncalibrated scores mislead reviewers, and drift erodes performance quietly. The business needs a model whose threshold matches staffing and whose decisions can be explained to reviewers and auditors.
users: Case reviewers who work the flagged queue
Operations managers who set review capacity
Model owners and risk or compliance reviewers

constraints.detail: The flagged volume must fit the daily review capacity.
Missed positives and unnecessary reviews carry different, explicit costs.
Each decision exposes its main contributing features.
Datasets, models, and thresholds are versioned; promotion requires recorded evidence.
Performance is reported across relevant segments before promotion.

zones.label: Promotion gate: registry stage change needs recorded approval

architectureNotes: The training pipeline refuses to run when leakage checks fail, such as features computed after the outcome date.
Thresholds are stored with the model version, so a model and its operating point are promoted together.
The challenger scores live traffic in shadow mode; its decisions are logged but not acted on until promotion.

aiTechnique.choice: Gradient-boosted trees against a logistic-regression baseline, with probability calibration and cost-based threshold selection.
aiTechnique.rationale: Tabular decision data is well served by boosted trees, and a linear baseline shows how much complexity buys. Calibration makes scores usable as probabilities so the threshold can be derived from costs and capacity.

rejected.reason: No evidence of benefit on moderate-size tabular data, and harder to explain.
Less accurate and less stable than trained models for structured prediction, and costly per decision.
Ignores imbalance, capacity, and asymmetric error costs.

implementation.detail: DVC-versioned datasets with time-based splits and automated leakage tests.
Stratified cross-validation, class weighting or resampling compared, hyperparameter search.
Isotonic or Platt calibration chosen by reliability on held-out data.
Expected-cost curve and capacity constraint used to pick the operating point.
MLflow tracks runs, artifacts, SHAP summaries, thresholds, and stage transitions.
FastAPI prediction endpoint returning score, decision, and top feature contributions.
Feature and prediction drift reports; scheduled retraining that registers but never auto-promotes.

datasets: A public or synthetic tabular dataset with a realistic positive rate and a time field

metrics.name: PR-AUC
metrics.target: Candidate vs baseline on the out-of-time holdout

metrics.name: Calibration error (ECE)
metrics.method: Expected calibration error over fixed bins

metrics.name: Expected cost at capacity
metrics.target: Cost per period at the chosen threshold vs default threshold
metrics.dataset: Out-of-time holdout with stated cost assumptions
metrics.method: Sum of false-negative and review costs under the capacity limit

regression: Leakage tests on every training run
Promotion blocked if the candidate underperforms the champion on the holdout or any monitored segment
failureAnalysis: Error review by segment and by top SHAP features
Drift episodes traced to feature sources

humanControl.detail: A model owner approves registry stage changes using the recorded comparison.
Reviewers see the top contributing features for each flagged case.
Retraining produces candidates; people decide what goes live.
Performance by segment is reviewed before promotion.

expected: Lower expected cost at the capacity-based threshold than at the default threshold
Improved calibration after isotonic or Platt scaling

limitations: Cost figures are illustrative assumptions, not a client's real economics.
Public or synthetic data does not reproduce every production pattern.
SHAP values explain the model, not causality in the world.
Segment fairness analysis is limited to fields available in the dataset.

setup: docker compose exec trainer python -m pipeline.train --config configs/default.yaml
docker compose exec trainer python -m pipeline.evaluate --holdout out_of_time
reproduction.testData: Dataset fetched or generated by data/README.md instructions and versioned with DVC.
reproduction.credentials: None required; MLflow UI runs on localhost.
reproduction.expectedOutput: MLflow runs for baseline and candidate, calibration plots, cost curve, SHAP summary, and a promotion recommendation.
